summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1 of 2: TOMMY (Joseph Hocking, 1916)

**Front matter:** Author's Note: he met "Tommy" before enlistment while addressing recruiting meetings; visited France/Flanders (La Bassée, Neuve Chapelle, Ypres); story is fiction in setting, fact in tale. Dedicated to families praying for soldiers. Dated Priors' Corner, Totteridge, Herts, Feb 1916.

**Ch I (Sunday, first Sunday in June 1914, Brunford, Lancashire cotton town):**
- Tom Pollard (~23, weaver's son, Dixon Street) leaves home ~3:30pm, Brunford Town Hall clock chimes. Goes to Thorn and Thistle pub (landlord Enoch Powell).
- Polly Powell, ~24, buxom, bold-eyed, highly coloured dress, landlord's daughter, flirts; mentions Jim Scott, Jim Dixon, Jim Parkin (gossip), says father would back Tom to start a mill; Tom took 3 prizes at Mechanics' Institute.
- Tom had promised a Tackler's job. Gave up Sunday School. Meets Alice Lister (~20, refined, contralto singer, daughter of George Lister, small manufacturer, mother Mrs. Lister) at Liverpool Road/Scott's Park. Alice gives ultimatum: give up Thorn and Thistle or her. Tom chooses Polly/Waterman.
- Emily Bilson mocks Tom. Harry Waterman (tall, florid, claims squire's son from Warwickshire, educated in Germany) invites Tom to "club" at Rose and Crown; scoffs at religion. Harry Briarfield (manufacturer's son) mentioned as Alice's suitor.
- Alice: "Duty, God." Leaves: "I see that your choice is made."
- Tom drunk that night; mother Martha Pollard scolds ("brazen-faaced 'uzzy"). Father Ezekiel Pollard.

**Ch II (June 1914–Jan 1915):**
- Dinner-party talk of war; Shweitzer (German townsman) at Bull and Butcher banquet predicts Kaiser ruling England; Englishman punches him, breaking jaw.
- Enoch Powell: "six weeks." Tom refuses to enlist; cites Polly. Waterman says he is getting a commission; says English will lose.
- Elijah Butterworth (son-in-law type, three sons in army) challenges Tom.
- New Year 1915 recruiting meeting at Mechanics' Institute hall; speaker (who had been in Belgium) says "Who will be the first?" Tom shouts "No! By God, no!" and enlists. Mother: "Ay, tha mun be sent to Lancaster asylum."

**Ch III:**
- Tom tells Polly; she says "I never thought much of soldiers." Meets Alice Lister next morning; she praises him ("we shall be praying for you"); he jokes about young parson.
- Joins Loyal North Lancashires (battalion unnamed, Lancashire town ~30 miles away). Drinks, disgraced, punished by colonel (stern, kindly). Robert Penrose (Cornish, public school, Charterhouse, gentleman ranker, refuses commission at first, later gazetted), urges Y.M.C.A.; French class; Tom recites "Je suis / Vous êtes / Nous sommes / Ils sont."
- Alec McPhail (Scottish, Black Watch, drinks whisky, Shorter Catechism, read Ingersoll; girl named Alice servant). Tom attends Y.M.C.A.
- Tom visits Brunford on leave; Polly sweet; he drinks. Battalion to Surrey camp (May 1915), Waterloo; Penrose's old school Charterhouse seen near Godalming. Tom meets Waterman as lieutenant in camp ("Yes, Mr. Waterman"). Mother's letter (Ch IV) says Polly walking out with Jim Dixon, Polly is "just the image of her mother," Tom should sack her.

**Ch IV:**
- Surrey camp life; Tom's French report; Y.M.C.A. praised. McPhail drinks at wayside pub. Embarkation at Folkestone; Boulogne; troop train; Ypres salient. Farewell Y.M.C.A. meeting: speaker says men need personal Saviour. McPhail and Tom at canteen; McPhail gives heart to God.

**Ch V (Ypres, late 1915):**
- Sergeant (served ~20 years, two bullets wounds, Ypres 1st/2nd battle, poison gas stories, Belgian shelling; German shot after surrender story). Tom in trenches "Piccadilly, Haymarket, Bond Street, Whitehall" trench names. Lancashire boy killed by sniper for raising head.
- Bayonet fight; young officer who fetched German officer wounded, shot dead by German with revolver (incident footnoted as true).
- Tom on sentry: "O God! O God!" prayer; thinks of Jim Bates, Arthur Wadge, Bill Perkins, George Wilson (dead pals). Waterman seen again by canal.

**Ch VI:** Alice refused Mr. Skelton (young minister). Harry Briarfield proposes; Alice asks days to think. Mr. and Mrs. Lister (George, "Our Alice"); Mrs. Lister's secret: once refused William Pott. Alice prays at midnight, "O God, save him!"

**Ch VII:** Night ~1am: German voice from trench warns of attack at 6am, 1100 men (Lancashires). Tom reports to subaltern, then Colonel; Sergeant Ashworth vouches for Tom. Attack repulsed by Black Watch. Tom's conversion: real God. Alec McPhail wounded; Tom visits hospital near road to Cassel; McPhail dies: "It's a' richt." Tom sings "Jesu, Lover of my soul"; they recite Psalm 23.

**Ch VIII:** Colonel Blount and Major Blundell; General Withers (Divisional HQ), Brigadier; leaks. Tom watched; sees Waterman (captain/staff officer) with Captain Winfield. Night: Waterman throws paper with white gleam and a "peculiar cry" toward German lines. Tom seizes him; Penrose (now lieutenant) intervenes. Tom crawls into No-man's-land, grapples with German, breaks his shoulder blade by football trick, returns with paper, shot in left arm and right shoulder. Major Blundell: "you've done the trick." Brunford friend Nick (Ay, Tom). Colonel Blount visits; Tom to give evidence.

**Ch IX:** Court-martial. Waterman admits: German at heart, parents German (name spelled with two n's, "Waterman" originally German-spelled), "Germany first." Shot at dawn against a wall; stands erect. Tom to get D.C.M. recommendation.

**Ch X (late Nov–Dec 1915):** Newspapers "Heroism of a Lancashire Lad." Mother's gossip: Alice engaged to Harry Briarfield (false later). Ezekiel: "Our Tom has give up that sort o' thing." Tom on leave to Brunford (December, Saturday); arrival at station crowd cheers; Polly at station with "I have not got any young men"; Tom refuses Rose and Crown ("following the example of the King"). Family kneels in prayer.

**Ch XI:** Chapel Sunday night with parents. Meets Alice in vestibule; walks her home up Liverpool Road. Alice: never engaged to Harry or Mr. Skelton. Tom: "will you wait for me, Alice?" "I can't help waiting for you." Mr. Lister approves grudgingly; Mrs. Lister: "yon's a grand lad." Tom's leave ends; Waterloo station with Alice; Kipling "ship that found herself"; "au revoir." Narrator saw him off. Closing: he will "fight on."

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: ADVENTURES OF BINDLE (Herbert Jenkins, c. 1917)

Dedication: "To the Children of the Dead End." Contents chapters I–XVI (Coming of the Lodger; Downing Street Sensation; Air-Raid; Duplication of Mr. Hearty; Gathering of the Bands; Mr. Gupperduck's Mishap; Courting of Rev. Andrew MacFie; Chapel Conversazione; Letting of Number Six; Downfall of Jabez Stiffson; Camouflaging of Gupperduck; Tragedy of Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino; Return of Charlie Dixon; Mr. Hearty Yields; Billeting Adventure; Millie's Wedding).

**Characters:** Joseph (Joe) Bindle, furniture remover, special constable, Fulham, cricket cap, pipe, calls wife "Mrs. B."; Lizzie (Mrs. Bindle), chapel-goer, Fenton Street, Fulham, sister of Martha; Alfred "Alf" Hearty, greengrocer (Putney, Fulham, Wandsworth shops), pious, wheezy; Martha Hearty (wheezes, breath, fat); Millie (Millikins) Hearty, niece, sweetheart Charlie (Sergeant Charles) Dixon, 110th Service Bn London Regt; Josiah Gupperduck, lodger, accordion, camouflaged; Rev. Andrew MacFie (Scots, "Mrs. Beendle"), sister Miss MacFie; Rev. James Sopley (retiring, "woe and whiskers"); Lady Knob-Kerrick (Barton Bridge, The Poplars, Putney Hill), companion Miss Strint, footman John (Calves), butler Wilton, Mrs Marlings; Ginger (red-haired, spits, dislikes twins), Wilkes (always coughing), Huggles, Tippitt (cigarette, taciturn), Scratcher, Ruddy Bill, Dick Little and brother Tom, "Guggers" (Captain, Gordons), Nancy Dane (Pierrette); Charlie Hart (porter, Fulham Square Mansions); Mrs. Sedge (Royal Richard gin); Cissie Boye (actress, Kiss Me Quick); Jabez Stiffson & Mrs. Stiffson; Oscar (canary); Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino (Napolini's waiter); Herr Smith / James Smith (superintendent); Chief-Inspector Gunny; Llewellyn John (Downing Street); Harry Gaze, Edgar.

**Ch I:** Mrs. Bindle answers ad "Christian home wanted" by Josiah Gupperduck (chapel-goer, temperance, musical/accordion). Bindle jokes; lodger arrives Monday.

**Ch II (Downing Street sensation):** Bindle rides horse for Empson & Daley; van to 110 Downing Street (Llewellyn John) with carved-oak furniture; Bindle fills roof with lampblack; suffragettes ("Black and White Raiders") in van; inspector; Chief-Inspector Gunny praises him.

**Ch III (Air-raid):** Bindle as special; Hearty and Gupperduck hide in potato cellar; Bindle drops scales; Mrs. Bindle faints. Millie: "Uncle Joe."

**Ch IV (Duplication):** Six Hearty "alibis" (doubles) appear in Hearty's new Putney shop; Dick Little/Guggers plan publicity; bands and donkeys, camel, "Pineapple Alf."

**Ch V:** Rival bands invade shop; inspector; "Gathering of the Bands."

**Ch VI:** Gupperduck beaten at peace meeting in Hyde Park; Bindle gives him whisky; Mrs. Bindle attacks Bindle.

**Ch VII:** MacFie courts Millie; Bindle exposes; Bindle's Bible quip re Uriah.

**Ch VIII:** Conversazione at Chapel school-room; "Glad Eye" glee; Alice Lister (maid, not Lister) announces guests; Lady Knob-Kerrick presents purse; woman claims MacFie as husband (Bindle's ruse with police whistle, Nancy Dane disguise).

**Ch IX:** Bindle as porter; Number Six let to Jabez Stiffson; Cissie Boye in same flat.

**Ch X:** Stiffson's double-booked flat; Mrs. Stiffson porridge; lift stuck.

**Ch XI:** Gupperduck at Hyde Park; "camouflage"; Ginger.

**Ch XII:** Bindle waiter at Napolini's; Tolmenicino arrested under DORA.

**Ch XIII:** Millie & Charlie Dixon; Bindle takes them to Universal Cafe; wedding urged.

**Ch XIV:** Bindle's trick to Hearty (blackmail-style story of Mrs. Hearty's "fairy tale"); Hearty yields.

**Ch XV:** Pantechnicon of 16 soldier bedsteads to Lady Knob-Kerrick's drawing-room; red herring; Lady K's rage.

**Ch XVI:** Millie's wedding (Alton Road Chapel, Mr. Sopley officiates); pineapple; Bindle's toast; Mrs. Dixon: "you must be a very good man."
